title: Couples note (F7) attributes statements to the right partner
hypothesis: Sam bought the bike; Alex felt left out — the note keeps that straight.
data:
Attendance and presentation
Clients Sam and Alex attended the 60-minute couple session. Both partners presented engaged, though affect was initially elevated during discussion of recent conflict.

Each partner's perspective
Alex raised concerns regarding financial decision-making and a perceived lack of inclusion, specifically noting feeling left out and that their opinion does not matter following an unconsulted purchase by Sam. Sam acknowledged Alex's perspective, clarifying that they were previously unaware of the deeper emotional impact and had misinterpreted Alex's response as solely anger about the monetary amount.

Relational patterns
The couple demonstrated a reactive cycle where financial stress triggered frustration and mutual escalation. Underneath the surface anger regarding monetary expenditures, vulnerability emerged regarding feeling excluded and misunderstood in decision-making.

Interventions
Encouraged pacing and slowing down the interaction during escalation Guided Alex in expressing primary emotional experience ('felt left out') rather than focusing exclusively on partner actions Facilitated perspective-taking and empathy regarding underlying emotional needs Assisted the couple in establishing a concrete financial communication rule

Plan
Implement the agreed-upon rule that purchases over two hundred dollars must be discussed first Continue weekly check-ins focusing on primary emotions and vulnerable communication Focus next session on reviewing the application of the new financial agreement and ongoing relational patterns
